actions.action: Inspect leaf undersides and stem joints with a magnifier or macro camera, including looking for webbing
Wipe a leaf with a white paper towel to check for mite smears
Isolate the plant from other plants
Wipe all leaves (tops and bottoms) and stems with soapy water or 50/50 diluted rubbing alcohol
Dab visible scale or mealybugs with a cotton swab dipped in straight alcohol
Spot-test the insecticidal soap or neem oil on one leaf first
Treat with insecticidal soap or neem oil every 5-7 days for 3-4 weeks
Rinse the plant in the shower
Move the plant out of the floor vent's airflow
Filter the light with sheer curtains for 1-2 weeks, then gradually move it to brighter light
Check the soil and water thoroughly when the top 2-3 inches are dry
Optionally trim badly browned leaf edges
If the infestation is heavy, apply a systemic insecticide

reason: The answer firmly identifies a pest infestation plus move and light stress, and its isolate, alcohol-wipe, soap/neem and optional systemic plan matches what the poster did; nothing in it is harmful.
